cards.title: Talk Less, Listen More: Giving Good Advice
cards.body: Before offering advice, ask yourself if your experience is relevant and if the person actually wants solutions or just to be heard. Experts reveal that people often seek advice simply to talk through their feelings, not to receive answers.

cards.title: The Girl With a Will to Live: Raising Elsie
cards.body: A parent shares their journey raising a daughter with an ultra-rare genetic disorder, describing the biggest campaign of their life. The article explores love, hope, and the challenges of caring for a child with life-threatening medical needs.

cards.title: Middle-Class Parenting Neglects Essential Life Skills
cards.body: Young people heading to university often lack basic skills like laundry and cooking, revealing gaps in family education. Parents should teach practical life competencies before children leave home.

cards.title: The Kindness of Strangers: When Parenting Goes Wrong
cards.body: A parent's child becomes sick in the car during a motorway journey, and a stranger's act of kindness provides help in an overwhelming moment. The story highlights how community support can ease parenting crises.

cards.title: Location-Tracking Apps and Parental Anxiety
cards.body: Parents using tracking apps struggle with constant surveillance of loved ones, unable to resist checking their location. The article explores the balance between safety and letting go.

cards.title: Suburban Life: Finding Joy in Family Neighborhoods
cards.body: A family discovers that suburban living offers unexpected opportunities for connection and community that they initially overlooked. The article shows how neighborhood engagement can transform a family's quality of life.

cards.title: Pre-University Shopping Reveals Parenting Gaps
cards.body: Taking a teenager to Ikea to buy dorm essentials exposes what domestic wisdom parents have failed to teach. The experience highlights a critical moment before children leave for university.

cards.title: How Children Learn Best
cards.body: The answer to how students learn most effectively is surprisingly intuitive. Understanding learning science helps parents and educators support children's development.

cards.title: How Do You Help a Child With ADHD Be Happy?
cards.body: Children with ADHD can flourish by focusing on their strengths while addressing specific challenges. This approach helps parents support their child's wellbeing and development.

cards.title: When Your Needs and Your Child's Needs Conflict
cards.body: Parents face moments when meeting their own needs contradicts what their child wants from them. Sometimes choosing yourself is not only acceptable—it's necessary for family health.

cards.title: Middle Childhood Asks Something of Parents, Too
cards.body: As children enter middle childhood and become more independent, parents also experience their own developmental changes. Understanding this transition helps parents navigate their changing role.

cards.title: The Self-Aware Sports Parent
cards.body: Youth sports can bring out stress in both kids and parents, but understanding boundaries helps everyone thrive. Parents should help children understand they are more than their athletic achievements.

cards.title: PowerBars and Other Signs the Empty Nest Is Coming
cards.body: As children prepare to leave for college, parents reflect on the changes ahead and reassure themselves everything will be okay. The empty nest transition brings both hope and uncertainty.

cards.title: What Makes Trauma Survivors Turn Out Well?
cards.body: Children can break the cycle of generational trauma through resilience and support. Understanding what helps survivors thrive offers insights for parenting and healing.

cards.title: Learner Drivers Turn to YouTube and TikTok
cards.body: Young people use social media clips to save money on driving lessons, but instructors warn of misinformation online. Parents should guide teenagers toward reliable learning resources.
